record.name: Ad Astra Sky Supply
record.description: Ad Astra Sky Supply is a defense sustainment startup focused on keeping aging military platforms ready: producing certified parts for ground, air and space systems, from prototypes to full-scale runs, and bringing legacy assets into the digital age with digital engineering. It has an alliance with Wichita State University's National Institute for Aviation Research (NIAR) to build a domestic supply chain spanning digital engineering, advanced manufacturing, testing and certification, and works with the DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory, with a cooperative R&D agreement planned. A woman-owned, veteran-led company founded by CEO Caroline Canfield in Prairie Village, Kansas, it launched at the 2025 Paris Air Show.
record.source: Wichita State NIAR release (Aug 13 2025); company site, Sep 2026; buildlist (founding year)
record.insight: The Pentagon spends most of a weapon's lifetime cost keeping it running, and parts for old platforms are often out of production. It's very early, so contract wins through NIAR and the Army lab will show whether the model works.
